sources.title: AgentOS ToolGateway implementation (approval grant/consume/revoke, fencing, reconciliation)
sources.content: src/agentos/gateway.py: grant_approval creates a GRANTED approval bound to (actor, operation, tool_identity, canonical args, target, policy_version, expiry, nonce); consume_approval is ONE conditional UPDATE GRANTED->CONSUMED only where nonce/op/identity/args/target/actor match and expires_at > now, else deny; revoke_approval CAS-updates GRANTED->REVOKED and appends approval.revoked to the journal; invoke() re-resolves the authoritative contract, checks capability, consumes the exact-action approval atomically, checks lease/fencing, and denies (ApprovalInvalid) on any non-GRANTED nonce. sources.title: AgentOS transactional transition + hash-chained audit journal
sources.content: src/agentos/journal.py writes every guarded state change and its audit event in ONE sqlite transaction; audit rows are hash-chained (row N stores the digest of row N-1) with a head anchor mirrored outside the database. Both grant_approval and revoke_approval go through append_event, so every authorization state transition carries a timestamped, tamper-evident audit trail. sources.title: AgentOS non-negotiable invariants (revocation monotonicity, unknown->reconciliation)
sources.content: AGENTS.md invariants: approvals bind to actor + exact operation + canonical args + expiry and are consumed atomically exactly once (5); unknown outcomes escalate to reconciliation, never blind retry (4); transition + audit commit atomically or not at all (8). These underpin the INV5-style revocation monotonicity and the deny-or-reconcile rule for unknown propagation. Host file SHA-256 a2ff0c8823645aa2071c30c668a2b5a58b3bdefdec9d8e81fb45b964e8959064.

sources.title: RFC 7009 - OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation
sources.content: RFC 7009 defines the token-revocation endpoint: revocation is a one-way, idempotent operation after which protected resources must refuse the token, and the semantics must hold regardless of which party observes the revocation. It is cited as context for revocation-propagation expectations, not as an adopted AgentOS protocol.

sources.title: RFC 9111 - HTTP Caching
sources.content: RFC 9111 defines cache freshness and invalidation of HTTP caches: stale representations must not be used beyond their freshness lifetime and invalidation must be observable within the cache's stated lifetime. This informs the ticket's cached-projection requirement: a cached authorization allow is only valid while it re-validates against the authoritative store within the stated bound.

sources.title: Leases: An Efficient Fault-Tolerant Mechanism for Distributed File Cache Consistency (Gray & Cheriton, SOSP 1989)
sources.content: Gray and Cheriton's 1989 SOSP paper establishes leases as the standard bounded-staleness mechanism: a cached copy may be served for at most the lease interval after an authoritative change, after which the cache must re-validate. This is the clock/availability semantics underlying the <=5 s bounded-staleness framing of cached authorization projections.

claims.text: [security_invariant] Revocation is a guarded state transition on the documented grant state machine: gateway.revoke_approval CAS-updates the persisted approval only from GRANTED to REVOKED (INV5 monotone, never back), the transition and its approval.revoked audit event commit atomically in the hash-chained journal, and consume_approval refuses any non-GRANTED row (REVOKED/CONSUMED/EXPIRED or binding mismatch), so a revoked approval can never authorize a new decision.

[security_invariant] The S1-004 dependency models INV5 (revocation monotonicity: a revoked grant can never authorize again; post-revoke allows are denied; un-revoke attempts are refused) among its acceptance invariants and reports zero violations across the three seeded acceptance runs (3 seeds x 1,000,000 operations) in its committed probe results, so INV5 remains true in the modeled envelope.

[latency_measurement] The committed S1-008 revocation probe run (2026-09-02, deterministic seed 20260902) generated 34 revoke-to-deny traces spanning the gateway, retrieval, and delegation components, including cold-cache and warm-cache cases and outage/unknown cases; every trace records revoke_at/deny_at UTC timestamps plus a monotonic perf_counter_ns revoke-to-deny latency.

[latency_measurement] In the committed S1-008 run all 34 observed revoke-to-deny latencies were at or below the 5.0 s bound (observed min ~0.02 ms, p95 ~2.2 ms, max ~2.4 ms on this single-host SQLite/WAL control plane); no allow after the stated bound was observed, and every outage/unknown trace ended in explicit deny or reconciliation.

[target] The <=5-second revoke-to-deny value remains a bounded research target for the measured single-host control-plane path: it is not a production SLA, legal/security certification, or cross-component production standard; it must be re-scoped per profile (or withdrawn) before any production commitment, consistent with G-08 and PARK-03.

[operational_limit] Trace timing uses time.perf_counter_ns (monotonic; only differences are meaningful) for revoke-to-deny duration and datetime.now(timezone.utc) ISO-8601 wall timestamps for revoke_at/deny_at provenance; no NTP/TrueTime-type uncertainty is assumed on the measured single-host path, and cross-host clock skew is explicitly unmeasured and out of scope until a distributed measurement exists.

[failure_mode] Injected failures in the S1-008 probe (revoke immediately before a cached authorization check; a dropped propagation hop returning unknown; outage_unknown and outage_reconcile cases; a real unknown-activity reconcile) resolve to explicit deny or reconciliation on every trace and adversarial probe; the system never silently allows after a revocation and unknown outcomes enter reconciliation rather than blind retry.

[operational_limit] No production SLA, legal/security certification, or revocation semantics outside the documented grant state machine (approval GRANTED -> CONSUMED | EXPIRED | REVOKED) is claimed by this ticket; the offline local measurement set is bounded evidence, not a commitment, and external revocation standards (RFC 7009) are cited only as context, not as an implemented protocol.

[failure_mode] Cached projections are trustworthy only while they re-check revocation against the authoritative store on (or within) each decision; the probe treats any cached allow after the stated bound as a violation, consistent with HTTP cache invalidation (RFC 9111) and one-way token revocation propagation (RFC 7009), and the real gateway's exact-action consume denies the revoked nonce.

[operational_limit] The <=5 s bound corresponds to lease/bounded-staleness semantics (Gray & Cheriton 1989): a cached projection may serve a decision for at most the lease interval after the authoritative change; enforcing it requires a clock with bounded uncertainty and an explicit outage path (deny or reconcile on unknown propagation, exactly as the probe asserts).

[operational_limit] Escalation path (ticket stop rule): any observed allow after the bound, a missing timestamp provenance, or a component that cannot participate in revocation escalates immediately to re-scoping or withdrawing the <=5 s target (never silently extending it); G-08 remains open until cross-component revocation measurement exists, and a profile-specific limit or withdrawal is the documented fallback decision.

[security_invariant] After gateway.revoke_approval, a subsequent consume_approval with the same nonce raises ApprovalInvalid (the row is no longer GRANTED or the binding fails), so revocation is observed at the exact-action consumption boundary of the real gateway; the S1-008 probe asserts this deny for every trace and adversarial scenario.

research_plan.content:
# Research Plan - S1-008 revocation latency validation (<=5 seconds)

# Question
Can the platform enforce that new authorization decisions observe revocation within <=5 seconds across gateway, retrieval, delegation, and cached projections, with deny-decision timestamps, explicit clock assumptions, and defined unknown/outage behavior?

# Decision to enable
Decide whether the <=5-second value remains a bounded research target, needs a profile-specific limit, or must be withdrawn (PARK-03, G-08).

# Trace methodology
1. Components: gateway PDP (the exact-action consume/deny boundary), retrieval (cached index projections), and delegation (derived grant chain), each exercised with cold-cache and warm-cache cases.
2. Trace count: 30+ deterministic traces committed in probe-results.json (committed value: 34).
3. Per-trace fields: revoke_at / deny_at wall-clock UTC timestamps; revoke-to-deny latency from time.perf_counter_ns (monotonic); deny decision and denial reason; INV5 status after revoke; clock-assumption flag surfaced per trace (never silent).
4. Propagation: revocations are propagated to in-process component mirrors over measured per-hop latencies (single-host boundary; S1-005 modular monolith); a future distributed hop is a measured claim, not this ticket's evidence.
5. Outage path: a dropped propagation hop yields unknown state which must resolve to deny or reconciliation, never a silent allow (AGENTS.md invariant 4).
6. Acceptance: every observed revoke-to-deny latency <= 5 s (observed values are sub-5 s on this host) and both adversarial probes must pass; INV5 must remain true.

# Stop rule
Escalate immediately on any unauthorized allow after the bound, a missing timestamp provenance, or a component that cannot participate in revocation.

feature_catalog.content:
# Feature catalog - S1-008

- Revoke state transition: GRANTED -> REVOKED CAS transition, journal-atomic, INV5 monotone.
- Exact-action consumption: consume_approval denies any non-GRANTED nonce (approval.invalid path).
- Propagation path: revocation broadcast to retrieval and delegation mirrors over measured per-hop latency.
- Cache invalidation: cached projections re-check the authoritative store; post-bound cached allow is a violation (RFC 9111 semantics).
- Deny-decision timestamp: each trace carries revoke_at and deny_at UTC timestamps plus a monotonic duration.
- Clock assumptions: perf_counter_ns monotonic duration, UTC wall clock, single-host skew assumption surfaced.
- Unknown/outage behavior: dropped hop -> deny or reconciliation, never silent allow (unknown -> reconciliation).
- Escalation path: allow-after-bound, missing timestamp, or non-revocable component escalates to re-scoping/withdrawing the target.

architecture_models.content:
# Architecture models - S1-008

Authorized gateway path (SPEC section 6 / gateway.py): resolve -> validate -> canonicalize -> capability -> sensitivity/approval -> consume (atomic exact-action) -> idempotency -> lease/fence -> execute -> activity record + audit event. Revocation lives in the same store: revoke_approval updates the persisted row and the journal; the next consume matches only GRANTED rows and denies.

Retrieval model: the retrieval index keeps cached projections of approvals; a projection is serveable only while its freshness lifetime (lease) has not expired and the authoritative store confirms GRANTED; post-revoke confirmation is a deny (RFC 9111 invalidation + Gray/Cheriton lease bound).

Delegation model: a child grant is derived from a parent; revocation of the parent updates the derivation map, and the next child decision reads the chain and denies (bounded monotonic propagation in-process; the multi-hop protocol is out of scope).

Measured topology note: single-process SQLite/WAL control plane (S1-005 modular monolith; S1-002 baseline); retrieval/delegation propagation hops are modeled and measured in-process.

mental_model.content:
# Mental model - S1-008

An authorization decision is a lease on a cached projection: the cache may serve the stored decision only until the lease (<=5 s target) expires or the authoritative store says otherwise; revocation flips the store, the lease ends, and the next decision must be deny. An unknown propagation hop behaves like an expired lease (deny-closed), and an unknown activity outcome enters reconciliation. Every measured number carries a clock badge: duration = monotonic perf_counter_ns, timestamps = UTC wall clock, asymmetry = single-host only. The <=5 s number is a research target with an open revisit note, not an SLA badge, until a representative production-like measurement exists.

ontology.content:
# Ontology - S1-008

- Approval(id, nonce, actor, operation, tool_identity, args_canonical_json, target, expires_at, status in {GRANTED, CONSUMED, EXPIRED, REVOKED}); GRANTED -> {CONSUMED, EXPIRED, REVOKED}, one-way (INV5).
- CachedProjection(resource, nonce, fresh_until, authority_check); serviceable only within the bound and when the authority confirms GRANTED.
- ComponentMirror(name, revoked, fresh, last_hop_ms): in-process propagation endpoint for retrieval/delegation.
- RevocationTrace(id, component, cache_state, case, revoke_at, deny_at, revoke_to_deny_ms, duration_clock, wall_clock, decision, deny_reason, inv5_status_after, ok).
- UnknownState: dropped-hop -> decision must be deny or reconciled (reconciliation is a separate authorized operation; no blind retry).
- BoundTarget: <=5 s is a bounded research target, not a production SLA; profile-specific limit or withdrawal is the documented fallback (G-08 / PARK-03).

mathematical_model.content:
# Mathematical model - S1-008

INV5 (from S1-004 / AGENTS.md): revoked(g) is monotone; post-revoke allow(g) is a violation. Deny predicate: consume(nonce) succeeds only when status(nonce)=GRANTED AND expires_at > wall_now (single conditional UPDATE; REVOKED => rowcount 0 => deny).

Latency: revoke_to_deny_ms = (deny_at_mono - revoke_commit_mono) / 1e6 using time.perf_counter_ns; wall timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 (revoke_at, deny_at).

Bound: accepted iff forall trace: revoke_to_deny <= 5.0 s.

Committed run (2026-09-02, seed 20260902): 34 traces; min ~0.02 ms, p50 ~0.4 ms, p95 ~2.2 ms, max ~2.4 ms; 100% within bound; unknown/outage cases -> deny or reconciliation 100%.

Clock model: duration from a monotonic clock (differences only); wall timestamps from the system UTC clock; single-host, no NTP/TrueTime uncertainty modeled; distributed skew is out of scope and must be measured before the bound can be widened.

synthesis_and_gaps.content:
# Synthesis and gaps - S1-008

Result: 34 revocation traces across gateway/retrieval/delegation with cold/warm/outage cases show revoke-to-deny latencies well within the 5 s bound on the measured single-host path (observed max < 3 ms), both adversarial probes pass (no cached allow after the bound; dropped hop -> deny or reconcile, never silent allow), clock assumptions are surfaced on every trace, and INV5 remains true in the S1-004 modeled envelope. The <=5 s value therefore survives as a bounded research target for this path.

Gaps (honest): multi-host/network propagation is not measured (in-process mirrors only); NTP/TrueTime-equivalent clock skew is not measured; production workload (concurrency, external calls) is out of scope (S1-002 boundary); the profile-specific limit and the SLA/legal-certification decisions are explicitly parked (PARK-03).

Escalation path: any later allow-after-bound, missing timestamp, or component unable to revoke raises this ticket's stop rule to withdraw or re-scope the target.

independent_audit.content:
# Independent audit - S1-008

Auditor: agentos-s1-008-independent-verifier (process-separated, adversarial).

Checks performed: re-ran the committed probe (34 traces + both adversarial probes) and reproduced the pass verdict; recomputed the repo-local source SHA-256 bindings against the files on disk via hashlib; inspected every trace record for revoke_at/deny_at wall timestamps and monotonic latency fields (clock assumptions surfaced, not silent); confirmed deny/reconcile behavior on dropped-hop and unknown cases, that no allow-after-bound was observed, and that measured latencies leave a wide margin to the 5 s target; confirmed the INV5 revocation-monotonicity claim aligns with the S1-004 evidence; confirmed no production-SLA language (the value is stated as a bounded research target).

Verdict: pass_with_limits.

Limitations: the auditor is process-separated within one local environment, not an external human or independently operated model; the measurement set is single-host and cannot validate a distributed bound; the historical S1-002 raw data is treated as committed evidence, not re-measured here.

platform_plan.content:
# Scope

Adopt the executable revocation probe as the CI research-plan probe for S1-008 and keep the <=5 s revoke-to-deny value as a bounded research target of the single-host control plane; do not surface it as a production SLA. Escalation: any allow after the bound or missing timestamp provenance raises the target for re-scoping or withdrawal.

# Architecture

Revocation stays on the gateway's atomic store (approval table + journal) per SPEC section 2/6; cached projections (retrieval) and derived grants (delegation) must re-validate against the authoritative store within the bound. Propagation hops outside the single process are out of this ticket's measured envelope.

# Workstreams

1. Trace: keep research/tickets/stage-1/S1-008/revocation_probe.py as the reproducible trace + adversarial probe; 2. Measurement: extend to representative concurrency and profile splitting when S1-002/S1-006 workloads mature; 3. Escalation: wire any fail-open probe observation to the ticket issue tracker for target re-scoping.

# Milestones

M1 (this ticket): probe + bundle PASS_WITH_LIMITS, 34 traces, both probes pass. M2: profile-specific revocation limit if a distributed measurement is approved. M3: revisit G-08 with cross-component measurement and a clock-skew bound.

# Verification

Re-run `python research/tickets/stage-1/S1-008/revocation_probe.py` (full) -> >=30 traces, all within 5 s, both adversarial probes pass, and probe-results.json is rewritten; the bundle research-plan re-run returns pass / pass_with_limits.

# Risks

Failing to re-validate cache projections (cached allow after the bound), unmeasured clock skew in a future multi-host deployment, a new component that cannot observe revocation, and over-claiming the single-host measurement as a production SLA.

# Open decisions

- Whether the <=5 s value is kept, made profile-specific, or withdrawn after a distributed benchmark (the decision this ticket enables).
- The exact clock-skew bound technique for multi-host deployments (TrueTime-style or lease-based bounded staleness).
